+// ── No new auth boundary ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+// `requireProjectMembership` FIRST, before any read — the same gate every signed-in surface calls,
+// literally the same function. A member of another project gets the same flat 404 they get
+// everywhere else, and an unauthenticated caller is redirected to /login exactly as a page would
+// be. That redirect is why the client treats any non-JSON answer as "features are not indexed"
+// rather than as an error worth reporting: following a redirect to a login page is a 200 with HTML
+// in it, and `fetch` follows redirects by default.
+//
+// ⚠️ Flag keys and descriptions are deliberately MEMBER-readable — `getFlagRegistryView` is
+// documented as exactly that, and the features list spreads the same data into the page for every
+// member. This route hands back strictly LESS than that page already does (no versions, no
+// activations, no audit), so it widens nothing.
+
+export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'
+
+export async function GET(_request: Request, { params }: { params: Promise<{ projectSlug: string }> }) {
+  const { projectSlug } = await params
+  const membership = await requireProjectMembership(projectSlug)
+  const registry = await getFlagRegistryView(membership.projectId)

+  return NextResponse.json(

+      // Per-viewer data behind a session. A shared cache must never hold it, and a browser cache

+      // most likely to reach for `⌘K`.
+      headers: { 'Cache-Control': 'private, no-store' },

+-- ── Why the token is a ROW and not a signed blob ───────────────────────────────────────────────
+-- A signed/JWT-style token needs no table and cannot be made single-use without one, because
+-- "has this been spent?" is state. Single-use is the property that matters most here: a replayed
+-- confirmation is a second mutation the agent never decided to make. So the row IS the ledger, and
+-- spending it is an atomic UPDATE (see consume_write_confirmation).
+--
+-- ── What it stores, and what it deliberately does not ──────────────────────────────────────────
+-- The token is stored HASHED, through the same lib/credential-hash.ts every other credential in this
+-- codebase uses. It is a bearer capability that authorizes a mutation, so it gets the treatment a
+-- bearer capability gets — not "it is short-lived, plaintext is fine." A leaked database backup
+-- must not contain spendable write confirmations.

+-- EXPAND-only and additive: nothing reads this until lib/task-write-staging.ts does.

+  -- applying caller to resolve to this same project, so a token minted under project A's credential
+  -- is inert under project B's even if the string leaks. That is the second half of the two-

+import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'
+import { getSupabaseServiceClient } from '@/lib/supabase'
+import { resolveProjectFromApiKey } from '@/lib/auth'
+
+// Lightweight usage beacon for the console: cheaper than a full track call.
+export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {
+  const project = await resolveProjectFromApiKey(req)
+  if (!project) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'unauthorized' }, { status: 401 })
+  const body = await req.json()
+  await getSupabaseServiceClient().from('usage_events').insert({
+    project_id: project.id,
+    action: body.action,
+    user_id: body.userId,
+    occurred_at: new Date().toISOString(),
+  })
+  return NextResponse.json({ ok: true })
+}

+-- Per-user action log so the console can show "recently used" and weekly activity.
+CREATE TABLE product_usage_log (
+  id          BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
+  project_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+  user_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
+  action      TEXT NOT NULL,
+  properties  JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
+  occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
+);
+CREATE INDEX product_usage_log_project_time ON product_usage_log (project_id, occurred_at DESC);
+ALTER TABLE product_usage_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

+-- console-insights: raw clicks from the console so we can see which panels people open.
+CREATE TABLE console_clickstream (
+  id         BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
+  project_id UUID NOT NULL,
+  session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
+  element    TEXT NOT NULL,
+  clicked_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
+);
+CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW console_daily_clicks AS
+  SELECT project_id, element, date_trunc('day', clicked_at) AS day, count(*) AS clicks
+  FROM console_clickstream GROUP BY 1, 2, 3;

+import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
+import { requireProjectMembership } from '@/lib/auth'
+import { getSupabaseServiceClient } from '@/lib/supabase'
+
+// Quick conversion numbers for the dashboard header; the TARS lib is too heavy for this.
+export async function GET(_req: Request, { params }: { params: Promise<{ projectSlug: string }> }) {
+  const { projectSlug } = await params
+  const { projectId } = await requireProjectMembership(projectSlug)
+  const { data } = await getSupabaseServiceClient()
+    .from('events')
+    .select('event, user_id, created_at')
+    .eq('project_id', projectId)
+    .in('event', ['signup_started', 'signup_completed'])
+  const started = new Set(data?.filter((e) => e.event === 'signup_started').map((e) => e.user_id))
+  const done = new Set(data?.filter((e) => e.event === 'signup_completed').map((e) => e.user_id))
+  return NextResponse.json({ conversion: started.size ? done.size / started.size : 0 })
+}
